resolvedQuestions.text: RQ-1: For each of the 16 skills, which parts of its routing section are agent-facing prose and which are machine data (assignment blocks, pseudocode, resource lists), and what is the word count of each part?

RQ-2: What loads these skills (OpenCode through opencode.json, Claude Code through .claude/, the Claude Project sync loop in 'AI Systems/z - Claude Project Sync Loop' and its hand-written knowledge files, and any other runtime), and does each loader load a file beside SKILL.md on its own?

RQ-3: Which check, benchmark gate or script in the AI Systems repository reads a SKILL.md routing section or a ROUTER.md, with file:line, and which of this repository's tools (package_skill.py, the router resolver) apply there?
RQ-4: How does each of the four existing ROUTER.md files classify against the new canon, and what does each need?

RQ-5: What is the per-skill migration design: target shape per skill, Claude Project knowledge-file changes, token saving per skill, and the order that avoids colliding with other sessions working in that repository?

keyFindings.text: **`opencode.json` names no skill path at all.** Its whole surface is `$schema`, `permission`, one `mcp.code_mode` entry and one `experimental` flag. There is no `skills`, `instructions`, `agents` or `references` key, so OpenCode is not told about a single one of the 16 skills. [SOURCE: opencode.json:1]

**The same gate already reads its pseudocode fence from a sibling file, which is the precedent phase 008 can copy.** `ROUTER_CONTRACT_MD` is `sk-sales-communication/references/router-contract.md` and `extract_pseudocode` compiles the fence out of it, while the prose guard still reads `SKILL.md`. Barter - Deal Templates does the same and says so in its header: "The prose guards keep reading their tables out of SKILL.md, because those tables ...", with the fence in `references/`, and a third copy `## 12. ROUTER CODE` inside the kernel. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Sales - Direct Communication/benchmark/router/differential.py:96] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Barter - Deal Templates/benchmark/router/differential.py:21] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Barter - Deal Templates/benchmark/router/differential.py:117]

**The Product Owner hub gate forbids a packet from owning a `ROUTER.md` and requires its routing to stay in `SKILL.md` section 2 - the exact opposite of the canon.** `PACKET_RESIDUE` lists `ROUTER.md` (line 58), `SMART_ROUTING_SECTION = re.compile(r"^## 2\. SMART ROUTING\n(.*?)(?=^## )")` (line 62) is applied at line 185 and a miss appends "packet SKILL.md has no Section 2 SMART ROUTING" (line 187). The same gate also pins the hub's own `ROUTER.md` with `router_state: active` (line 55) and `skill_pointer: SKILL.md` (line 56). [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:58]

**`check_leaf_map_parity.py` reads the hub `ROUTER.md` Python block and each packet's `SKILL.md` `RESOURCE_MAP`, so it spans both homes today**: `source = (ROOT / "ROUTER.md").read_text()` then `DEFAULT_RESOURCE, RESOURCE_MAP, INTENT_SIGNALS` (lines 72-75), against `(ROOT / packet / "SKILL.md")` and its `RESOURCE_MAP` (lines 88-91). [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_leaf_map_parity.py:72]

**Four Moneybird gates read `ROUTER.md` as a first-class surface, which makes those three skills the working model for the move.** `check-skill-words.py` counts `COUNTED_NAMES = ("ROUTER.md", "SKILL.md")` with the three router files listed as exemptions (lines 54-64); `check-route-table.py` "Reads the ROUTER.md beside the skill's SKILL.md" (line 7) from `ROUTER_MD = os.path.join(SKILL_FOLDER, "ROUTER.md")` (line 63) and can regenerate the router block (line 35); `route-replay.py` replays `ROUTER.md` (lines 8, 77); `exit-code-parity.sh` reads `TROUBLESHOOT` keywords out of `cli-moneybird/ROUTER.md` (lines 45, 230). [SOURCE: AI Systems/Moneybird Accountant/sk-moneybird-accountant/scripts/check-skill-words.py:54] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Moneybird Accountant/sk-moneybird-accountant/scripts/check-route-table.py:63] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Moneybird Accountant/cli-moneybird/scripts/exit-code-parity.sh:45]

**This repository's router-shape tooling is vendored into AI Systems but scans `.skilled/skills`, so it does not currently police the 16 project skills.** `ci-router-vocabulary-reach.cjs:50` and `generate-router-intent-signals.cjs:30` both set `SKILLS = path.join(REPO_ROOT, '.skilled', 'skills')`, and `routing-shape-known-debt.json` is keyed by path under `.skilled/skills` with 4 entries. **The vendored `package_skill.py` is not the same tool as this repository's: its RS codes are swapped, so a code number means different things in the two repositories.** The AI Systems copy reports `RS-004` as "mode packet carries its own ROUTER.md" / a missing sibling router (lines 1006-1008) and `RS-005` as "no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section" (line 1000), while this repository's copy reports `RS-004` as "no sibling ROUTER.md beside SKILL.md" (line 1029) and `RS-005` as the missing pointer link (line 1113). A migration plan that cites codes without the repository will be read backwards by whoever runs the other copy. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1000] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1029]

**`.opencode/skills` is a symlink out of the repository and holds none of the 16.** It resolves to `/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills` and lists 17 entries (`cli-classifier`, `cli-external-orchestration`, `cli-orca`, `local-obsidian`, `local-webflow`, `mcp-code-mode`, `mcp-tooling`, `sk-code`, `sk-communication`, `sk-design`, `sk-doc`, `sk-git`, `sk-prompt`, `system-deep-loop`, `system-skill-advisor`, `system-spec-kit`, `README.txt`). [SOURCE: .opencode/skills]

**`.claude/skills` is a symlink to the same Public tree, not to `AI Systems/`.** Claude Code therefore loads the same 17 shared skills and, like OpenCode, never sees the 16 project skills. [SOURCE: .claude/skills]

**The load path that does reach the 16 is one command, and it reads exactly one file: `{skill_folder}/SKILL.md`.** `Commands/agent-router.md` step 4 says it "Finds and reads the COMPLETE skill identity (the named `{skill_folder}/SKILL.md` that AGENTS.md points to)", its table row 3 records `skill_path, skill_content`, and its load rule says "Primary: read `{agent_scope_root}/{skill_folder}/SKILL.md` COMPLETELY. On load, its routing, references and assets define the identity. Then load only what `SKILL.md` marks ALWAYS". No sibling file is named anywhere in that path. [SOURCE: Commands/agent-router.md:50] [SOURCE: Commands/agent-router.md:329]

**No loader in the repository reads a file beside `SKILL.md` on its own, so a sibling `ROUTER.md` is invisible until `SKILL.md` links it.** That is the load-bearing fact behind the canon's pointer rule: the router can move, but the link in `SKILL.md` is the only thing that brings it back in. [INFERENCE: from findings 1-4 plus the absence of any `ROUTER.md` reader in the two runtime symlink trees]

**Claude Projects have no automated path at all: the sync compiler was retired on 2026-09-18 and Project files are hand-written.** `AGENTS.md` section 5 states the compiler "is retired and its folder was deleted on 2026-09-18", that a change means listing skill files against their Project counterparts, updating the matching kernel or knowledge file "by hand or record that no Project-facing change is needed", and that "No manifest, lock file or checksum ledger is kept". [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:119]

**The sync loop's residency ledger shows a hand migration already in flight, counted in statements rather than files.** `residency/counts.md` records 98 of 327 declared statements moved (0 interlock, 16 every-answer, 34 route, 48 duplicate-or-machine), and `residency/moved-route-*.json` keeps per-system statement keys. Anything phase 008 changes in a kernel has to be reconciled with this ledger or it will read as drift. [SOURCE: AI Systems/z — Claude Project Sync Loop/residency/counts.md:1]

**The Sales differential gate slices the routing section out of `SKILL.md` by literal heading, so the prose cannot leave without the gate.** `prose[prose.index("## 2. SMART ROUTING"):prose.index("## 3. HOW IT WORKS")]` raises `ValueError` the moment either heading moves. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Sales - Direct Communication/benchmark/router/differential.py:268]

**All four existing routers carry the same two frontmatter fields, and a gate pins both.** `router_state: active` and `skill_pointer: SKILL.md` sit at Product Owner lines 11-12 and at lines 10-11 in each of the three Moneybird routers; `check_hub.py` pins them as `ROUTER_STATE_LINE` and `SKILL_POINTER_LINE`. Any restructure keeps those two lines byte-identical. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:11] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Moneybird Accountant/cli-jortt/ROUTER.md:10]

keyFindings.text: **Recommended way for a Project to receive a router: one new versionless knowledge doc per System that needs routing, holding the `## MACHINE ROUTER` payload verbatim, with the kernel reduced to a pointer plus its interlock rules.** The name follows the existing convention, for example `Sales Direct Communication - System - Routing.md`; the kernel keeps only the rules that must hold on every request and names the doc in its always row; the change is recorded as a dated parity note in the system `SYNC.md`, per `AGENTS.md` section 5. This satisfies REQ-003 and it is the only shape that keeps the kernel and `ROUTER.md` comparable, because the doc can be diffed against the router block word for word. [INFERENCE: from findings 8-9 and the `<System> - <Section> - <Title>.md` convention]

keyFindings.text: **The order that avoids collisions runs from the quiet, gate-free skills to the hot, gate-bound ones, and puts each gate change in the same commit as the skill it guards:** Media Editor (no differential gate, mtime 2026-10-05, 258 machine words) pilot; Prompt Improver (quiet since 2026-10-18); Barter - Copywriter (quiet since 2026-10-18, and the only table-shaped router, so it proves the shape without a fence); Sales - Direct Communication (its `differential.py` prose slice changes in the same commit); Sales - HubSpot & Automation (gate lives under `specs/`, quiet since 2026-10-01); Barter - Deal Templates (differential gate plus the kernel `## 12. ROUTER CODE` copy, touched 2026-10-27); the Moneybird cluster (heading rename plus `check-route-table.py --write` before the hand edit, hub pointer added, quiet repository); the Product Owner cluster last (four MCP/FigJam packets and the hub, with `check_hub.py`'s residue rule relaxed first, then the hub `ROUTER.md` restructure, then the packets). [INFERENCE: from findings 2-5, 11 and the iteration-1 and iteration-2 gate inventory]

ruledOutDirections.text: Counting routing words with `wc -w` over the raw section. It inflates fenced blocks and tables, because punctuation and markdown markers collapse into fewer tokens than my tokenizer produces: `wc -w` reads 8,213 words for `sk-barter-copywriter` while the tokenizer reads 8,018 for the whole file. Rejected in favour of one consistent tokenizer, and the rule is stated above so phase 008 can reproduce the numbers.

Reading `### Executable Contract` as a machine-data marker. In `sk-barter-copywriter` (line 232), `sk-barter-deal-templates` (line 115) and `sk-media-editor` (line 126) that heading holds plain prose describing the contract, not the contract itself. A heading-name heuristic would misclassify all three.

Treating the whole `SKILL.md` as "the routing section". The spec's measured behavior anchors on `## .*SMART ROUTING`, and every other section (WHEN TO USE, RULES, RESOURCES, DELIVERY) is skill content that the move must not touch.

Searching for a skill loader in `opencode.json`. There is no skill key to extend, so the only way a sibling router reaches a runtime is the `SKILL.md` pointer and the agent's own follow-the-link behaviour.

Assuming a packaging script will rewrite a Claude Project from the skill source. `AGENTS.md` section 5 retires the compiler and forbids a manifest, lock or checksum, so the Project update is a hand edit or a recorded "no change needed".

Assuming `.claude/skills` or `.opencode/skills` holds the 16 project skills. Both are symlinks into `Code_Environment/Public` and hold the same 17 shared skills; the project skills are reached only by `Commands/agent-router.md`.

Reading the AI Systems `specs/` harnesses (`AI Systems/Sales - HubSpot & Automation/specs/.../harness.py`, `AI Systems/Barter - Deal Templates/specs/.../harness.py`) as live gates. They live under `specs/`, which the topic excludes, and the replay is kept under `benchmark/`.
Renaming `## 2. SMART ROUTING` to `## MACHINE ROUTER` in place. It leaves prose inside the machine section (finding 4) and, for Product Owner, leaves two sections after it (finding 3).

Giving every Claude Project the repository's `ROUTER.md` verbatim. Product Owner's router is 1,229 words and `sk-moneybird-accountant`'s is 2,435, which would move cost into every Project retrieval rather than cut it; the residency class work in iteration 2 already shows that shape being rejected by hand.
Migrating Product Owner first because it is the most visible. Its commit cadence (daily) and its packet gate make it the worst first target.
Looking for an existing Project routing doc to extend. There is none, so the first one is an authoring decision and belongs in phase 008's plan rather than a find-and-replace.
